llm.summary: The skill is a disclosed self-hosted speech service, with real privacy and deployment risks that are explained rather than hidden.

dimensions.detail: Outbound HTTP to TALKIES_URL, optional MCP, and local shell examples are expected; users should restrict network exposure, enable bearer auth outside trusted local use, and avoid debug logging with real user data.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Setup uses Docker images, host bind mounts, model downloads, curl, and optional ffmpeg, which are proportionate for this service but require normal container provenance and command review.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions are user-directed examples and repeatedly warn agents to use only trusted servers, avoid unauthorized voice cloning, avoid browsing or deleting other users' staged files, and perform model eviction or cleanup only for explicit workflows.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Server-side staged files, URL-download caches, model data, and custom voices persist under the server data directory and lack per-caller isolation, but the artifact clearly discloses this and gives cleanup and access-control guidance.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The documented capabilities, including transcription, text-to-speech, voice cloning, server-side URL fetching, MCP access, and staged file management, fit the stated purpose of operating a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible speech API.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intend to run or trust the talkies server. Enable TALKIES_AUTH_TOKEN and limit port exposure for any shared or non-local deployment, do not process confidential audio/text through an untrusted TALKIES_URL, clean up staged files and cached URL downloads, avoid debug logging with real data, and use voice cloning only with explicit speaker consent.
llm.findings:
[LP4] expected: The declared network permission is supported by the artifact's curl examples, TALKIES_URL configuration, TTS/ASR calls, and documented server-side URL fetching, so this is not unmatched authority.
[SQP-3] expected: The Japanese/Chinese Kokoro limitation is documented as a missing optional dependency/runtime support issue, not as a hidden policy or security behavior.
[E1] expected: The speech endpoint examples send TTS text to TALKIES_URL; that external transmission is necessary for a remote/self-hosted TTS API and is prominently disclosed.
[E1] expected: The custom voice example sends text and uses a configured voice sample through the local or configured talkies server; the artifact also warns to use only authorized voices and trusted servers.
[E1] expected: The later TTS workflow examples repeat the same expected API behavior and do not add hidden destinations or unrelated telemetry.
[E1] expected: The setup reference uses localhost in the flagged example, consistent with a self-hosted deployment, not undisclosed exfiltration.
[EA2] expected: The quoted consent language is a safety warning for voice cloning, not evidence that the skill enables autonomous destructive or high-impact decisions without user control.
